definition: A diagram in the $(x, y)$ plane showing the trajectories of a pair of coupled differential equations, with arrows for the direction of motion as time increases; time itself is not an axis.
The path a solution $(x(t), y(t))$ of a pair of coupled differential equations traces in the $(x, y)$ plane as $t$ increases.

A point where $\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = 0$ and $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = 0$ at the same time, so a solution that starts there stays there; for $\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = ax + by$, $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = cx + dy$ with non-zero eigenvalues it is the origin only.

An equilibrium point of a linear system whose eigenvalues are real with opposite signs: trajectories come in alongside the negative eigenvalue's eigenvector line and leave alongside the positive one's, so it is unstable.

An equilibrium point that all nearby solutions move towards as time increases; for $\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = ax + by$, $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = cx + dy$ the origin is stable when both eigenvalues are negative or complex with negative real part.
